expect.note: Findings #59-#60: `campaign start level:grumpstone_ridge` fails outright (tier-2, locked by default -- same class as Finding #58/the already-documented treranium_depths issue), so this file runs against the substitute new_game world throughout; not fixed here for the same reason. `employee assign_skill` used the same rejected positional syntax as Finding #45/#54 -- fixed to `skill:geology level:N`. All 5 of the `build` commands (`office`/`storage_depot`/`canteen`/`medical_bay`/`break_room`) name nonexistent building types, matching the established Finding #5/#47/#58 no-op pattern -- left unmarked rather than fixed, consistent with precedent. A `debris_hauler` is bought (along with a rock_digger and drill_rig) but never assigned a driver and never sent on a single `vehicle haul` -- despite 4 real blasts, `storedMassKg` stays 0 for the whole file and all 5 contract deliveries fail honestly for lack of storage; not fixed here either, since the hauling mechanism is already proven end-to-end by `level1-playthrough-win.json` and re-proving it here would cost the same again for no new verification value (Finding #59). Unusually for this batch, the file's own hardcoded contract IDs (1, 2, 3, 4, 5) all happened to match the real, currently-available pool at every listing -- no ID-mismatch fix was needed here, unlike every other multi-cycle-contract file this session. Finding #52's drill-grid class recurred a 4th time across all 4 of this file's grids (declared 12/16/20/20 holes vs. real 24/25/30/48) -- fixed the same way. The corrected, far larger grids are violent enough to kill 2 employees during the very first blast (deathCount 0→2, tick 32) -- a real, reproducible consequence, not a scenario bug. Discovered while investigating an unexplained $10,000-per-cycle income jump in `finances` output despite every delivery failing: some random events (at least `lucky_strike`) resolve silently and instantly inside a `tick` call -- the tick command's own output says 'No events fired' even as the event's transaction (`category:'contracts', description:'Event: lucky_strike'`) is added to the finance log -- a materially different mechanic from every other file's pending-choice events (`[tick N] EVENT: Name` + a required `event choose`). Because this file has real (if silent) events firing, `cash` is hard-asserted only through tick 32 (the first such event) and left unasserted after that, per Ground rule #12/Finding #34's established treatment, rather than assumed safe just because no `event choose` step was ever needed (Finding #60). No bankruptcy, revolt, or ecological shutdown within this file's 62-tick budget -- cash ends around -$67k but never crosses the sustained-100-tick grace threshold; safety and nuisance both bottom out at 0 from the accumulated real blast violence, matching the pattern from `level1-win-efficient.json`. Verified in both command mode and a real browser (interaction mode re-run twice for determinism, both clean), 108/108 steps.
